fields.statement: QA at f6e4af6e with a binary built from the branch, in a hermetic scratch repo (own HOME, RHIZA_* unset). rhiza session status-line fed Claude Code-shaped JSON (session_id, model, rate_limits five_hour 10% and seven_day 49%): exit 0, printed the user's own statusLine output (a printf+head command from HOME/.claude/settings.json, receiving the same stdin), --json said recorded 2, and .git/rhiza/usage.live.json held one session and one weekly snapshot with used_percentage, resets_at and captured_at. After rhiza root init on the parent dir the same command wrote to <root>/.rhiza-root/usage.live.json instead; a later input with only seven_day replaced weekly and left session. rhiza session start (fake rex) then rhiza session run <id> --dry-run --json: the claude argv's --settings JSON carries statusLine {type: command, command: '<rhiza path> session status-line'} beside the 7 hook events.

QA at f6e4af6e with the built binary: the recorded usage.live.json was read back by rhiza health and rhiza daemon --once (both report the snapshot-derived limits); replacing the file with garbage made health fall back to the settings (session 0 of 555; weekly 0 of 777) with exit status unchanged and no error, so a corrupt file gives no snapshots and stops nothing.

QA at f6e4af6e with the built binary under a scratch Rhiza root, one registered project, a fake transcript of 4900 counted tokens (cache reads excluded) 30 minutes old, and rhiza daemon set rhiza.daemon.usage.session 555 / weekly 777. With live snapshots 10% (5h) and 49% (7d) rhiza health showed 'session 0 of 49000; weekly 0 of 10000' (4900/0.10, 4900/0.49), not the settings. Live weekly 99% then rhiza daemon --once --permission-mode acceptEdits: the daemon held with a usage-reserve inbox item 'weekly window: 4900 tokens used, 4900 projected, over the limit of 4949 less a 20% reserve', and daemon.state.json's windows took reset = resets_at and start = resets_at minus 5h / 7d. Recording 49% and polling again cleared the hold (health 'session 4900 of 49000; weekly 4900 of 10000'). A session snapshot at 0.5% gave no live session limit (health fell back to 555) while weekly stayed live. Setting every resets_at in the past and polling fell back to the settings: hold on session at limit 555.
